chunk_findings.detail: After this change no code path in `_apply_config` ever calls `CW.apply_edit`: the only remaining write is `_remove_key` on the `knob_removed` branch, because `_writes_config` now requires `change == "knob_removed"` and every other item falls through to an `ACKNOWLEDGED` return. Concretely, with the repro from the ticket — project pins `worktree.max_parallel=4` (`set_by="file"`), new default `0`, item action `OPERATOR`, kind `knob_changed` — `ddflow upgrade --apply --confirm worktree.max_parallel` now returns `ACKNOWLEDGED` with "kept this project's value 4 (file)" and writes nothing. That inverts the semantics of the very flag the plan entry points at ("[needs operator confirmation] default changed 4 -> 0; this project sets 4 (file)"): an operator who *does* want the new default (e.g. the old value is deprecated, or the schema now rejects it) gets a success-looking status, no change to `.ddflow/config.toml`, and no `--keep`/`--adopt` alternative, so the item can never be resolved toward the new default. The context's expected resolution was to add an explicit keep flag (or at minimum to say plainly in the plan text that `--confirm` adopts the new default); this change does neither, it silently redefines `--confirm` as "keep the pin" while leaving the misleading plan line untouched, which is the confusion the bug report asked to remove. Note also that the `pinned and kind == "knob_changed"` branch is not guarded by `item["action"] == UP.OPERATOR`, so even non-OPERATOR items now print the "kept … " message.

chunk_findings.detail: The change repurposes `--confirm KEY` for a project-pinned knob from "adopt the new default" to "acknowledge and keep the old value", and there is no longer any input that adopts the new default. The diff's own retained reason string proves the operator's stated intent is now ignored: the test invokes `go(old, "config", confirm={key: "the new default fits"})` — i.e. `upgrade --apply --confirm worktree.max_parallel --reason "the new default fits"` — and the new assertion demands that the run nevertheless report `acknowledged`/`kept` and leave `Config.load(old).worktree.max_parallel == item["old"]` (4), even though the operator explicitly confirmed that 0 "fits". The new regression test merely swaps the reason to `"keep my pin"` so the contradiction is hidden. Concretely: with a project pinning `worktree.max_parallel=4` and a new default of 0, the invocation the intent itself quotes (`ddflow upgrade --apply --confirm KEY --reason …`) now silently discards both the confirmation and its reason, and no other command shown in this diff lets the operator reach 0 through the upgrade flow — the changed assertion at line 923 (`[acknowledged] knob_changed:worktree.max_parallel`) confirms there is no remaining apply path for pinned knobs. The intent asked for an *additional* way to keep the pin (e.g. `--keep KEY`) and/or for the plan text to state plainly what `--confirm` does; instead an existing flag contract was inverted without updating the plan text (`"[needs operator confirmation] default changed 4 -> 0; this project sets 4 (file)"` still reads as if confirming decides the change), so the bug's silent surprise is replaced by the opposite silent surprise.

chunk_findings.detail: The new plan/apply text is gated on `operator_set` in the plan but on `set_by` (`pinned`) in `_apply_config`, and those are not the same set of items — the file's own docstring asserts they differ ("a knob at its shipped default takes the new default by itself, even when the policy makes the operator confirm it"). Concretely: a knob the project never set (`set_by` absent, so `pinned = False`) whose default changes (e.g. old default 4 -> new default 0) and whose policy makes it an `OPERATOR` item (`operator_set` true, since that is exactly the flag that drives the `--confirm KEY --reason ...` fix command in the lines right above). For that item the plan now renders `... (keeps this project's value; to adopt the new default: ddflow config --set KEY 0)`, but `_apply_config` skips the `pinned and kind == "knob_changed"` branch and returns `ACKNOWLEDGED, "<key>: the new default applies on its own; pin the old behaviour with ddflow config --set <key> 4"` — i.e. confirming *does* adopt 0 and the value changes, the exact opposite of what the plan just promised, and the opposite of the advice for keeping the value. An operator who confirms because the plan said the value is kept gets the value silently changed, which is the same class of misdirection the ticket was filed about. The appended text needs the same `set_by` guard the apply path uses (e.g. `if kind == "knob_changed" and item.get("set_by")`), or the two messages must be made consistent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new plan note that says `--confirm` "keeps this project's value" is gated on `operator_set` — the same flag that decides whether `item["fix"]` uses `--confirm` (visible in the hunk's `if operator_set else "ddflow upgrade --apply"`). That flag is the "policy requires operator confirmation" flag, not "the project pinned a value". `_apply_config` gates the same claim on a different condition: `pinned = bool(item.get("set_by"))` (upgrade_apply.py, `if pinned and kind == "knob_changed":`), and `_writes_config`'s own docstring explicitly contemplates a knob at its shipped default being routed through operator confirmation ("even when the policy makes the operator confirm it"). So for an item with `change == "knob_changed"`, `action == UP.OPERATOR`, and no `set_by` — e.g. default changed `4 -> 0` and the policy wants the operator to confirm it — the plan now tells the operator that confirming "keeps this project's value; to adopt the new default: ddflow config --set <key> <new>", while the actual apply path returns `ACKNOWLEDGED, "the new default applies on its own"` and the effective value becomes `0`. The note must be gated on `item.get("set_by")` (the `pinned` condition) to match what `_apply_config` actually does.

The note is now appended to `item["fix"]` for every `knob_changed` item with `operator_set` true, including items whose value is fixed by the environment. The sibling code this note is supposed to describe deliberately refuses exactly those items: `upgrade_apply.py` starts `_apply_config` with `if pinned and src.startswith("env") and item["action"] == UP.OPERATOR: return REFUSED, f"{key} is set by the environment ({src}); change it there"`. That refusal can only ever fire for an item with `set_by` truthy (the pre-change `_writes_config(item)` gate was `action == UP.OPERATOR and bool(item.get("set_by"))`, and the env check sat behind it), and `set_by` is only populated when `operator_set` is true — so an env-overridden pin is precisely an `operator_set` item that reaches this new note.

Concrete input: project config pins `worktree.max_parallel = 4` in the file layer, and an env var (e.g. `DDFLOW_WORKTREE_MAX_PARALLEL`) overrides it, so `src == "env…"`; upstream changes the shipped default to 0. The plan item is `knob_changed` with `operator_set` true, so the plan now prints `… (keeps this project's value; to adopt the new default: ddflow config --set worktree.max_parallel 0)`. But confirming that item returns `REFUSED … set by the environment (env…); change it there`, i.e. it is not resolved and no value is kept at all, and the advertised remedy `ddflow config --set …` is a no-op for adoption because the environment override still wins. The operator is handed two commands that can neither resolve the item nor adopt the new default — the guidance contradicts the apply's own "change it there". The note (and the "keeps this project's value" claim) needs to be excluded when `src.startswith("env")`, or the plan should state plainly that the value is fixed by the environment.
